body_markdown:
A nationwide recall involving Cuisinart metal wire grill brushes has expanded significantly, with more than 3.6 million products now included because of a potentially serious ingestion hazard.


Conair, the company responsible for Cuisinart-branded grill brushes, announced an expanded recall on Aug. 27, 2026, after reports that small metal bristles can break away from the brushes and remain on grill grates or food. If swallowed, the loose wires could cause serious injuries to the mouth, throat, digestive tract or other internal organs.


The latest action adds about 1.9 million brushes to a recall announced in July. According to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, approximately 3,625,800 Cuisinart grill brushes are now covered by the two recalls.


## Why Are the Cuisinart Grill Brushes Being Recalled?


The problem involves the metal wire bristles used to clean grill grates.


During use, individual bristles can detach from the brush. The small wires may then remain on the grill surface or become attached to food without being noticed. Consumers who unknowingly eat the bristles could face serious internal injuries, according to federal safety officials. Some injuries may be severe enough to require surgery.


Conair has received at least 54 reports involving detached bristles, according to the CPSC. Three of those reports involved consumers who swallowed metal wires and required medical treatment to remove the bristles from their digestive tract or throat.


The issue is particularly concerning because the bristles can be extremely small and difficult to see before food is served.


## More Than 20 Models Are Included


The expanded recall covers numerous Cuisinart grill brushes and grill tool sets.


The newly added models include:


- CGWM-024
- CGWM-059
- FCB-501
- CGS-W18
- CCB-134
- CGWM-061
- CB-395
- CCB-3001
- CGWM-077
- CGWM-058
- CCB-012/021
- CGWM-060
- FBH-51


These join models included in the earlier July recall, including CCB-100, CCB-4125, CCB-5014, CCB-6450, CCB-8012, CCB-4114, CCB-W2 and CSBS-777.


The recalled products have been sold with different handle designs, including black plastic, stainless steel and wooden handles. Some were sold individually, while others were included as part of larger grill tool sets.


Among the affected sets are the Premium Grill 10 Piece Set, 13 Piece Wooden Handle Grill Tool Set, 14 Piece Deluxe Stainless Steel Grill Set and 20 Piece Deluxe Grill Set. Consumers should check the model information on their products rather than relying solely on the appearance of the brush.


## Where Were the Recalled Products Sold?


According to the CPSC, affected Cuisinart grill brushes were sold through major retailers and online stores.


Retailers named in the recall notice include Walmart, Burlington, TJ Maxx and Ross. The products were also sold online through Amazon and Cuisinart's website.


The affected brushes were sold from June 2009 through March 2026, with retail prices generally ranging from approximately $8 to $20.


Because the recall covers products sold over many years, consumers should not assume that an older grill brush is safe simply because it was purchased long ago.


## What Should Consumers Do?


The CPSC advises consumers to stop using the recalled grill brushes immediately.


Consumers should check their grill brushes and tool sets for the affected model numbers. If a product is included in the recall, it should no longer be used for cleaning a grill.


Conair is offering a full refund or a credit for use at Cuisinart.com. According to the CPSC, consumers who choose the credit can receive a full refund plus an additional 20 percent of the cash refund amount. Consumers will be instructed to discard the recalled brushes.


Consumers can find the official recall information and instructions through the CPSC recall notice and the recall contact information provided by Conair.


## Cuisinart Is Not the Only Grill Brush Recall This Year


The Cuisinart recall is part of a broader series of recalls involving metal wire grill brushes in 2026.


In March, Nexgrill recalled more than 10.2 million metal wire bristle grill brushes sold at Home Depot. The CPSC cited the same basic hazard, warning that small metal bristles can detach from the brush, remain on the grill or food, and potentially be swallowed.


Earlier, in February, Weber recalled more than 3.2 million metal wire bristle grill brushes. The CPSC again warned that detached bristles could cause serious internal injuries if swallowed. The agency reported cases involving consumers who required medical treatment after ingesting metal bristles.


These recalls highlight a broader safety concern associated with wire-bristle grill cleaning tools. Consumers who regularly use such products may want to check whether their particular brush has been subject to a recall, even if it is not a Cuisinart, Nexgrill or Weber product.


## Why This Recall Matters


Grill brushes are generally inexpensive household products, which can make a recall involving millions of units seem surprising. However, the potential consequences of a detached metal bristle are much more serious than the cost of the product itself.


A wire bristle that remains on a grill grate can be difficult to detect. If it becomes attached to food, a consumer may have no practical way of knowing it is there before taking a bite.


The Cuisinart recall therefore serves as an important reminder that seemingly routine kitchen and outdoor cooking accessories can present safety risks when components break or detach during normal use.


Consumers should also avoid giving recalled brushes to another person or selling them secondhand. A recalled product should be handled according to the manufacturer's instructions.


## What About Other Wire Grill Brushes?


Consumers who own wire-bristle grill brushes from other manufacturers should check the CPSC's recall database for current safety notices.


The CPSC's 2026 recalls involving Nexgrill, Weber and Cuisinart demonstrate that the issue is not limited to one product line. The agency has specifically warned about the danger posed by metal bristles that detach and become embedded in food.


If you have recently used a recalled brush and believe you may have swallowed a metal bristle, seek appropriate medical attention. Do not attempt to diagnose or treat a possible internal injury yourself.


## Bottom Line


The expanded Cuisinart recall affects approximately 3.6 million grill brushes and follows millions of other wire-bristle grill brushes recalled in the United States this year.


If you own a Cuisinart grill brush, check its model number against the official recall list before using it again. If your brush is included, stop using it and follow Conair's instructions for obtaining a refund or credit.


With grilling season underway, taking a few minutes to check a grill brush could help prevent a potentially serious injury.

### Disclaimer


This article is provided for general informational purposes and is not medical, legal or product-safety advice. Recall information can change, and consumers should verify the latest details directly with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and the manufacturer before taking action. If you believe you have been injured by a recalled product, consult an appropriately qualified medical or legal professional.
